title: A Roof Inspection Before You List
description: Buyers and inspectors will look up. A photo report before you list tells you what they are about to find.
html:
The buyer’s inspector has an hour and a ladder. You have the weeks before the sign goes in the yard. Those weeks are when a small repair is still a small repair, and when a tired roof can be priced into the sale instead of blowing up the option period.

What shows up in an option period

Missing tabs, cracked boots, stained decking in the attic, and a seller who says “it has never leaked.” Buyers do not need a collapsed ceiling to ask for a credit. They need a photo of a soft valley and a contractor who will put a number on it. If that number arrives on day eight of a ten-day option, you are negotiating from behind.

A roof inspection before you list is the same photo set we would give a buyer, done while you still control the calendar. If the roof is sound, you have something to hand the other side. If it is not, you can repair the detail, replace the roof, or price the house with the truth attached.

Do not hide hail

Fresh sealant over a bruised slope does not survive a careful walk. It also makes a later insurance conversation harder, because someone has altered the evidence. Document what is there. Fix what is worth fixing. Disclose what you know.

Repairs that photograph well

Replace cracked boots, reseat slipped step flashing, and clear valleys before the listing photos. Those are visible, cheap compared with a credit, and they show a house that has been kept. A full replacement, if that is the truth, should be finished or disclosed. A half-finished tear-off on picture day helps nobody.

Give the buyer the same photo set you used. Surprises in the option period cost more than the repair would have.

If you are listing in the Houston suburbs, request a free inspection before the photographer shows up. Call (281) 541-0027. If the answer is a replacement, the suburb replacement timeline shows how a one-to-three-day job fits between listing photos and the first weekend of showings.
